thread.title: The Ratings Game: Chip makers lead tech stocks lower even as Nvidia sees larger available data-center market

title: The Ratings Game: Chip makers lead tech stocks lower even as Nvidia sees larger available data-center market
text:
Published: Mar 28, 2018 4:41 p.m. ET Share 
Not even prospect of $50 billion data-center market cheers chip stocks Reuters Wallace Witkowski Reporter 
Shares of chip makers led the decline in tech stocks Wednesday even after Nvidia Corp. significantly raised its forecast of the potential data-center market going forward, and analysts suggested that Nvidia could be to the data center what Apple was for the cellphone. 
Nvidia NVDA, -1.85% shares fell for a second day, closing down 1.9% at $221.35, as the company hosted the final day of its GPU Technology Conference in San Jose, Calif. Shares dropped 7.8% Tuesday after the company halted real-world testing of self-driving cars after an Uber Technologies Inc. test car killed a pedestrian in a collision last week. 
Overall, the S&P 500’s tech sector slumped 0.9% on Wednesday while the broader index SPX, -0.29% was down 0.3%. Chip stocks weighed on the tech sector, as the PHLX Semiconductor Index SOX, -2.12% fell 2.1%. 
Intel Corp. INTC, -3.11% shares shed 3.1% to close at $49.60 while IHS Markit reported that Samsung Electronics Co. 005930, -2.56% had dethroned the Santa Clara, Calif.-based chip company for annual revenue leader. Samsung shares were down 2.6% Wednesday. 
Similarly, shares of Broadcom Ltd. AVGO, -3.15% , Marvell Technology Group Ltd. MRVL, -3.80% , Qorvo Inc. QRVO, -2.41% and Microchip Technology Inc. MCHP, -3.43% fell 2% or more. 
Read: Tech sector forfeits half a trillion dollars in value over 2-week span 
In a sign that tech stocks may be red-lining, the sector was soft even as Nvidia said Tuesday that it sees the long-term annual data-center market at $50 billion, up from its year-ago forecast of $30 billion, and analysts are seeing Nvidia as a major growth player because it’s built a popular ecosystem around its products in that arena. 
In February , Nvidia reported fiscal 2018 data-center revenue of $1.93 billion, a 133% increase from the previous year, its fastest growing segment that accounted for about 20% of its revenue. In comparison, automotive sales, which rose 15%, only accounted for $558 million in sales in fiscal 2018 revenue. 
Read: Will the tech rout wreck the stock-market rally? 
“What remains impressive, in our view, is the rate at which NVDA’s developer ecosystem related to these end markets is growing, which illustrates continued leadership and competitive advantage for NVDA’s platform strategy,” said Ruben Roy, MKM Partners analyst, in a note. Roy has a neutral rating on Nvidia and a $245 price target. 
Regarding the ecosystem, Nvidia’s chipsets run on the company’s CUDA parallel computing platform, so data centers that are buying into Nvidia’s chipsets are also buying into company’s software and libraries ecosystem. 
Saying that Nvidia is a graphics-chip company is like calling Apple Inc.’s AAPL, -1.10% iPhone an A11 processor, said Mark Lipacis, Jefferies analyst, in a note. Lipacis has a buy on Nvidia. 
“We think that the iPhone ecosystem is a relevant analogy for NVDA,” Lipacis said. 
Lipacis went on to note: 
NVDA spent a good part of its analyst day explaining about the investments it has made in its software and developer ecosystem, particularly focused on the limited set of markets where it expects to have a material impact: Autos, Healthcare, Robotics, Datacenter, Gaming, VR. In one chart NVDA showed that it had more software engineers than hardware engineers - our take - NVDA is not just a semiconductor company. 
Of the 32 analysts who cover Nvidia, 15 have overweight or buy ratings, 15 have hold ratings, and two have sell ratings, with an average price target of $250.93. Related Topics
